name: Question 17
problem:
Let the function $f(x,y)$ be defined as

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{y+1}{1+{x}^{2}},\, & \text{if}\,1<x<2,\,1<y<2, \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}},\, & \text{if}\,1<x<2,\,2<y<4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then,

$$
{∬}_{(1,2)\times (1,4)}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the rectangle $R$ can be represented as a union of two smaller rectangles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =(1,2)\times ((1,2)\cup (2,4)) \\  & =((1,2)\times (1,2))\cup ((1,2)\times (2,4)).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{(1,2)\times (1,2)}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{(1,2)\times (2,4)}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{(1,2)\times (1,2)}\frac{y+1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{(1,2)\times (2,4)}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Let the function f(x,y) be defined as f(x,y)={y+11+x2,if1<x<2,1<y<2,x2y2,if1<x<2,2<y<4. Then, ∬(1,2)×(1,4)f(x,y) dA=

a
 ∬(1,2)×(1,2)x2y2dA+∬(1,2)×(2,4)y+11+x2dA
b
 ∬(1,2)×(1,2)y+11+x2dA+∬(2,4)×(2,4)x2y2dA
c
 ∬(1,2)×(1,4)x2(y+1)y2(1+x2)dA
d
 ∬(1,2)×(1,2)y+11+x2dA+∬(1,2)×(2,4)x2y2dA
e
 ∬(1,2)×(1,4)(y+11+x2+x2y2)dA
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the rectangle R can be represented as a union of two smaller rectangles, as follows:

R=(1,2)×((1,2)∪(2,4))=((1,2)×(1,2))∪((1,2)×(2,4)).

So, we can write

∬Rf(x,y)dA=∬(1,2)×(1,2)f(x,y)dA+∬(1,2)×(2,4)f(x,y)dA=∬(1,2)×(1,2)y+11+x2dA+∬(1,2)×(2,4)x2y2dA.
